title: Re-Animator
note: Herbert West brings a very bad idea to medical school. The perfect doorway into messy, manic practical-effects horror.

title: Night of the Creeps
note: Alien slugs, college kids, and a wonderfully hard-boiled detective. A love letter to several monster-movie eras at once.

title: The Return of the Living Dead
note: Punk attitude, black comedy, and the worst possible warehouse accident. Keep the barrel closed. Seriously.

title: Killer Klowns from Outer Space
note: The circus has landed, and the popcorn is suspicious. Elaborate creature designs make this an ideal friends-and-pizza rental.

title: Chopping Mall
note: Security robots. A shopping mall. A very unfortunate overnight party. Produced by Julie Corman, this belongs on the Corman-family shelf.

title: Videodrome
note: A television signal gets under the skin. Cronenberg turns media obsession into a nightmare that feels wonderfully tactile and deeply unsettling.

title: The Fly
note: A scientific breakthrough becomes a devastating physical transformation. A strong second feature when you want body horror with an emotional punch.

title: Piranha
note: A Roger Corman production with Joe Dante at the helm. An excellent rental for a night of sharp teeth and gleefully irresponsible science.

title: The Little Shop of Horrors
note: The original, non-musical Corman film: a tiny flower shop, a very hungry plant, and a gloriously peculiar comic nightmare.

title: The Thing
note: The essential snowbound rental: distrust, isolation, and gloriously unsettling creature transformations.

title: Alien
note: A haunted-house night in deep space. Slow dread and industrial grime make this a cornerstone of the shelf.

title: Aliens
note: Follow the quiet dread of Alien with a full-throttle siege. A terrific change of pace for a long movie night.

title: Predator
note: Action-movie swagger meets a creature feature. Best rented when the room wants both explosions and a monster.

title: They Live
note: A scrappy Carpenter sci-fi nightmare with a sharp satirical streak. An ideal partner for a media-paranoia night.

title: The Terminator
note: An unstoppable pursuer gives this time-travel thriller a slasher heartbeat. Keep it in the late-night machine aisle.

title: RoboCop
note: Corporate satire, comic-book brutality, and a battered human core. A rental for the dark side of future technology.

title: Blade Runner
note: Neon-soaked science-fiction noir. A slower, moodier detour from the monster shelf, with several distinct versions to explore.

title: Pet Sematary
note: A bleak family nightmare from the Stephen King aisle. Save this for an evening that can handle the weight.

title: Night of the Comet
note: A playful apocalypse with mall-era personality. An ideal bridge between sci-fi oddities and horror comedy.

title: Galaxy of Terror
note: A Corman-produced sci-fi horror oddity. Adult exploitation content makes this a considered late-night rental.

title: House of Usher
note: Corman and Vincent Price bring a different kind of dread to the shelf. Earlier roots for the later video-store obsession.

title: The Pit and the Pendulum
note: A gothic Corman-and-Price stop for a velvet-and-cobwebs night. Pair with House of Usher for the earlier lineage.

title: The Blob
note: A gloriously gooey creature remake. Put this on when the evening calls for practical effects and a town-wide panic.

title: Critters
note: Tiny monsters, enormous appetites. A natural pick for a playful creature-feature night.

title: Gremlins
note: Holiday charm with a wicked little streak. A gateway rental for the mischievous end of the monster aisle.

title: Tremors
note: A desert town and a very bad reason to touch the ground. Easygoing character comedy makes the creature mayhem sing.

title: Pumpkinhead
note: A creature-feature rental with a folk-tale mood. Choose this for a darker monster night.

title: The Howling
note: A werewolf shelf staple with a sly streak. A strong starting point for a transformation-themed evening.

title: An American Werewolf in London
note: A wickedly funny nightmare with a transformation sequence worth building an entire evening around.

title: From Beyond
note: An excellent next rental after Re-Animator. Stuart Gordon pushes strange science into a wet, vivid nightmare.

title: Night of the Living Dead
note: The earlier zombie cornerstone. A powerful contrast with the faster, funnier undead chaos of the ’80s.

title: Scanners
note: Cronenberg turns psychic power into physical danger. A sharp addition to the science-gone-wrong shelf.

title: The Brood
note: A grim, intimate Cronenberg nightmare. Save this for a night that favors unease over popcorn-party camp.

title: The Dead Zone
note: A quieter Cronenberg rental with a tragic supernatural hook. A useful change of pace within the director shelf.

title: Society
note: Social paranoia with a truly outrageous payoff. Go in knowing as little as possible.

title: Basket Case
note: Grimy New York exploitation energy and a very unusual traveling companion. A must for the weirder end of the aisle.

title: Brain Damage
note: Frank Henenlotter turns a strange attachment into a grimy urban nightmare. A good companion to Basket Case.

title: Frankenhooker
note: A deliberately outrageous mad-science rental. Best programmed for an audience ready for very broad, very dark camp.

title: The Evil Dead
note: The cabin-in-the-woods rental that never behaves. Raw momentum and relentless supernatural chaos.

title: Evil Dead II
note: A slapstick haunted-house roller coaster. One of the easiest picks for a room full of horror fans.

title: Army of Darkness
note: The video-store era stretches into the early ’90s with an undead fantasy romp. Pair with Evil Dead II for the tonal ride.

title: Hellraiser
note: A puzzle-box rental with an unusually severe imagination. For nights when the store needs something darker.

title: Phantasm
note: A dreamlike funeral-home nightmare. Rent it for the strange atmosphere as much as the shocks.

title: The Fog
note: Carpenter makes a coastal ghost story feel like a campfire warning. A beautifully moody late-night choice.

title: Prince of Darkness
note: Science and supernatural dread collide inside a church. The ideal rental for an ominous, slow-building night.

title: Halloween
note: A patient suburban nightmare and a cornerstone of the slasher shelf. Let the atmosphere do its work.

title: Friday the 13th
note: Campground suspense from the formative video-store slasher years. A foundation tape for a whole franchise aisle.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
note: A slasher premise with a surreal playground. The perfect crossover between the nightmare and knife shelves.

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
note: A grimy ’70s root of the ’80s horror aisle. An intense rental that works best with room to breathe afterward.

title: Sleepaway Camp
note: A peculiar campground slasher. Keep the ending unspoiled and leave time for a conversation after the credits.

title: My Bloody Valentine
note: Mining-town atmosphere gives this slasher its own flavor. A great pick for a themed February rental night.

title: Poltergeist
note: Suburban comfort becomes supernatural spectacle. A strong rental for a big, crowd-pleasing haunted-house night.

title: The Shining
note: A long, cold descent into dread. Program it as the main event rather than rushing toward another feature.

title: Fright Night
note: A vampire movie with a horror-host heart. An especially fitting tape for the Neon Coffin counter.

title: The Lost Boys
note: Neon, vampires, and summer-night attitude. This belongs in the friends-and-pizza rotation.

title: Night of the Demons
note: A Halloween party that goes very wrong. A rowdy rental for the late-night supernatural shelf.

title: Dawn of the Dead
note: A shopping-mall apocalypse with bite beyond its zombies. A cornerstone pairing for a consumer-chaos evening.

title: Day of the Dead
note: A harsher, claustrophobic zombie rental. The opposite mood to a punk-comedy night with Return of the Living Dead.

title: Maximum Overdrive
note: A gloriously loud machines-gone-bad night. Put this next to Chopping Mall and keep the snacks moving.

title: The Stuff
note: A consumer-culture creature oddity. A natural partner for an evening of suspicious products and bad appetites.

title: House
note: An oddball haunted-house rental with comic energy. A lighter companion for an otherwise grim ghost night.

title: Elvira: Mistress of the Dark
note: Elvira takes the big screen. A perfect host-culture rental for a campy, personality-first movie night.

title: Bride of Re-Animator
note: Return to the laboratory for another very questionable project. An obvious sequel-night choice for Herbert West fans.

title: Humanoids from the Deep
note: A harsh Corman-produced creature exploitation rental. Its sexual violence makes it a deliberate adult programming choice.

title: Forbidden World
note: A Corman-produced space-monster rental for the B-movie aisle. A good choice when you want the scrappy side of deep-space horror.

title: Death Race 2000
note: A Corman-produced dystopian road-race satire. A gleefully abrasive detour into the ’70s drive-in roots.

title: Event Horizon
note: A later descendant of the haunted-spaceship aisle. A deliberate ’90s extension of the store’s core era.

title: In the Mouth of Madness
note: A ’90s Carpenter nightmare about fiction refusing to stay on the page. A fitting extension of the paranoia shelf.

title: Hardware
note: An abrasive cyberpunk rental with a grimy machine-horror mood. A strong fit for the neon end of the collection.

title: The Exorcist
note: A defining ’70s nightmare. Treat it as the evening’s main event and give the aftermath some room.

title: Carrie
note: A supernatural tragedy with a brutal high-school setting. An essential stop on the Stephen King shelf.

title: Child’s Play
note: A toy-store nightmare with a mean comic streak. One of the most recognizable tapes in the late-’80s aisle.

title: Christine
note: Carpenter, Stephen King, and a very possessive car. A natural partner for the machines-that-misbehave shelf.

title: Creepshow
note: Comic-book color and anthology-night variety. A terrific counter pick when nobody can settle on one kind of nightmare.

title: The Monster Squad
note: Classic monsters crash into an ’80s adventure movie. A nostalgic creature-night choice with a mischievous streak.

title: The Gate
note: A suburban monster nightmare from the younger end of the video-store aisle. Great for a small-scale effects night.

title: Motel Hell
note: Roadside hospitality with a very dark joke at its center. Keep it in the strange, grimy drive-in corner.

title: The Toxic Avenger
director: Michael Herz Lloyd Kaufman (as Samuel Weil)
note: Troma’s outrageous mutant mayhem. A deliberate choice for viewers who want their camp loud and abrasive.

title: Halloween II
note: The nightmare moves from Haddonfield’s streets to its hospital. Pair it with Carpenter’s original for one long, very bad Halloween night.

title: Halloween III: Season of the Witch
note: A standalone Halloween nightmare of sinister masks, television signals, and corporate witchcraft. A different story from Michael Myers, with its own wonderfully strange October atmosphere.

title: Trick or Treat
note: A dead rock star, a dangerous record, and a Halloween concert that should never happen. Pure heavy-metal video-store trouble.

title: Trick ’r Treat
note: A later seasonal essential: interlocking Halloween stories, jack-o’-lanterns, costumes, and Sam keeping an eye on the rules. Our deliberate modern exception for October.

title: Halloween 4: The Return of Michael Myers
note: Michael Myers returns to Haddonfield a decade later. A quintessential late-eighties Halloween rental: small-town streets, autumn shadows, and an old nightmare coming home again.

title: Halloween 5: The Revenge of Michael Myers
note: The fifth stop on our original Halloween shelf. Jamie Lloyd and Dr. Loomis face another Haddonfield Halloween with Michael Myers on the hunt.

title: Return of the Living Dead Part II
note: Another misplaced barrel, another town in trouble. The sequel cranks up the slapstick and brings the brain-hungry chaos back to the video-store counter.

title: Return of the Living Dead 3
note: Brian Yuzna takes the series into tragic romance and body horror. A darker rental for the night when punk zombies give way to heartbreak and practical-effects transformations.

title: Return of the Living Dead: Necropolis
note: The outbreak moves into a sinister research facility. A mid-2000s detour into corporate experiments, rescue missions, and very poor containment procedures.

title: Return of the Living Dead: Rave to the Grave
note: Trioxin crashes a Halloween rave. The fifth tape trades warehouse punk for party-night mayhem: glowing pills, loud music, and guests with a terrible appetite.

title: Sleepaway Camp II: Unhappy Campers
note: The summer camp sequel brings back Angela with a much meaner sense of humor. The right follow-up for fans of the original’s warped sleepaway-camp slasher energy.

title: Sleepaway Camp III: Teenage Wasteland
note: Angela returns for a rowdier, more openly comic third visit. Keep the double feature going after Unhappy Campers.

title: The Slumber Party Massacre
note: A lean, self-aware sleepover slasher with a sharp point of view and a very memorable power tool.

title: Slumber Party Massacre II
note: A surreal, music-soaked sequel that takes the slumber-party formula into dream logic and rock-video weirdness.

title: Slumber Party Massacre III
note: The trilogy closes with a new group of friends, a weekend house, and one more videotape-era stalker.

title: The Burning
note: A summer-camp grudge becomes a classic backwoods stalker picture. A natural rental after Sleepaway Camp.

title: Black Christmas
note: The original holiday-house slasher: chilly, tense, and enormously influential. File it under the roots of the babysitter-at-nightmare’s-door era.

title: Pieces
note: A wildly excessive, labyrinthine campus slasher made for the most outrageous end of the midnight shelf.

title: Prom Night
note: A disco-lit high-school slasher with Jamie Lee Curtis, a masked killer, and a reunion night that goes very wrong.

title: Intruder
note: A late-night supermarket becomes a remarkably inventive slasher playground. Look for Sam and Ted Raimi in the chaos.

title: The Prowler
note: A masked WWII-uniformed killer, a small-town dance, and effects work that made this one a video-store midnight staple.

title: Hell Night
note: Linda Blair and a haunted-house fraternity dare deliver an atmospheric campus slasher with a great rental-sleeve setup.

title: Dead Heat
note: A buddy-cop zombie comedy with practical-effects mayhem and peak late-night video-store energy.

title: Street Trash
note: New York grime, outrageous practical effects, and underground exploitation attitude. A deep-cut rental for a fearless crowd.

title: Evil Spawn
note: A scrappy low-budget creature feature with practical makeup and a late-night cast of genre regulars.

title: Vamp
note: Grace Jones presides over a neon-lit vampire club in one of the coolest, strangest urban creature features of the decade.

title: Spookies
note: A wonderfully unruly haunted-house oddity full of monsters, mud creatures, and handmade effects. Put it on with friends.

title: TerrorVision
note: A garish, gooey alien invasion by way of a satellite dish, with a wonderfully tacky family-TV aesthetic.

title: Rock n Roll Nightmare
note: A Canadian heavy-metal oddity that makes the video-store bargain bin feel like a portal to another dimension.

title: Necropolis
note: An obscure, scrappy witch-and-undead VHS discovery. This is the 1986 film, separate from Return of the Living Dead: Necropolis.

title: Blood Rage
note: A Thanksgiving slasher with twins, mistaken identity, and a line delivery that made it a cult holiday favorite.

title: The Dungeonmaster
note: A Corman-era fantasy-horror anthology with practical monsters, analog computers, and gloriously oddball visions.

title: Demon Wind
note: A handmade, effects-heavy demonic-house movie from the video-store era’s final stretch. Best watched with the lights low and expectations delightfully loose.

title: Sorority House Massacre II
note: A knowingly silly sequel from the bargain-bin end of the slasher cycle, directed by exploitation regular Jim Wynorski.

title: Blood Hook
note: A regional slasher with a fishing tournament, a small-town cast, and exactly the kind of oddball premise you want on a VHS shelf.

title: Doom Asylum
note: A punky, self-aware slasher set in an abandoned asylum, with bargain-bin atmosphere and a cast of familiar faces.

title: Class of Nuke ’Em High
note: Troma’s radioactive high-school freakout: mutant students, nuclear fallout, and the proudly unruly spirit of the label.

title: Surf Nazis Must Die
note: A post-apocalyptic revenge romp from Troma’s cult shelf. The title is the whole warning label.

title: Redneck Zombies
note: An independent Troma cult release with homemade gore, backwoods zombies, and an unmistakably DIY video-store identity.

title: Nightbreed
note: Barker’s dark fantasy opens a door to a community of monsters hiding beneath the ordinary world. A natural companion to Hellraiser.

title: Children of the Corn
note: Stephen King’s rural nightmare became an enduring video-store staple and launched a long-running series.

title: Silver Bullet
note: A Stephen King werewolf tale with a wheelchair-bound young hero, a small-town mystery, and classic creature-feature pleasures.

title: The Deadly Spawn
note: A tiny budget, a basement full of hungry offspring, and a gloriously elaborate creature design. The sort of handmade monster tape that made a late-night rental feel like a discovery.

title: Blood Diner
note: A Vestron-era splatter-comedy fever dream: a restaurant, a very bad family tradition, and a gleefully unhinged midnight tone. A perfect back-row discovery.

title: The Video Dead
note: A direct-to-video zombie oddity where the television itself becomes the doorway. It belongs on a VHS-culture shelf by title, format, and wonderfully analog premise.

title: Evilspeak
note: Clint Howard, a military-school outcast, and a very early computer-assisted occult nightmare. A notorious video-era curiosity with a distinct early-80s chill.

title: The Mutilator
note: A regional slasher with a seaside setting, an instantly recognizable video-era title, and the kind of blunt hook that practically sells the rental itself.

title: C.H.U.D.
note: A New York sewer mystery with practical monster work, grimy streets, and a title made for the video-store wall.

title: Puppet Master
note: Full Moon’s signature killer-puppet franchise begins with an isolated hotel, secret craft, and a perfect late-night rental hook.

title: Invaders from Mars
note: Tobe Hooper turns a suburban childhood into a bright, gooey alien-invasion nightmare, complete with striking practical effects.

title: Something Wicked This Way Comes
note: Ray Bradbury’s dark small-town fantasy brings a sinister carnival, autumn dread, and an unusually eerie Disney-era production.

title: Terror Train
note: A New Year’s party on a moving train, Jamie Lee Curtis, and a killer who keeps changing costumes: peak early-slasher VHS appeal.

title: The Funhouse
note: Tobe Hooper’s carnival-set nightmare turns a night of teenage mischief into a grimy, atmospheric creature feature.

title: Deadly Friend
note: Wes Craven’s oddball sci-fi horror mixes a gifted teenage inventor, a beloved robot, and a resurrection gone sideways.

title: Cat People
note: Paul Schrader’s lush, feverish reimagining pairs animal transformation myth with shadowy New Orleans atmosphere and Giorgio Moroder’s score.

title: The Entity
note: A severe, unnerving supernatural drama whose stark housebound imagery made it one of the era’s most discussed occult-horror rentals.

title: The Changeling
note: A grieving composer, a cavernous old mansion, and patient sound-driven dread: a refined ghost story with a true rental-shelf chill.

title: I Spit on Your Grave
note: A raw, confrontational revenge thriller that became one of the most notorious independent horror releases of its era.

title: Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer
note: A bleak, low-budget character study whose restrained style makes it far more unsettling than a conventional slasher.

title: Satan’s Blood
note: Spanish occult horror about a couple drawn into a ritual that opens a door they cannot close.

title: Slaughter High
director: George Dugdale, Mark Ezra & Peter Mackenzie Litten
note: A cruel high-school prank returns years later at a reunion in this colorful, effects-heavy slasher.

title: Near Dark
note: A moody road movie that fuses western imagery, family drama, and a distinctly nocturnal vampire myth.

title: The Stepfather
note: Terry O’Quinn anchors a sharp suburban thriller about a new husband whose polished persona hides a violent past.

title: Alligator
note: A city sewer legend becomes a practical-effects creature feature with a satirical bite.

title: Possession
note: An intense, surreal relationship drama that erupts into body horror and an unforgettable performance by Isabelle Adjani.

title: Wolfen
note: An atmospheric urban thriller blends police investigation, Native American mythology, and unusual animal-perspective imagery.

title: Dead of Winter
note: A suspenseful snowbound thriller follows an actress trapped in a remote house with a dangerous host.

title: The Hidden
note: A fast, funny science-fiction chase movie pairs an alien parasite with a hard-boiled Los Angeles detective.

title: Phenomena
note: A young student with an uncanny connection to insects investigates a series of killings in a dreamlike Swiss setting.

title: Bloody Birthday
note: A rare alignment of the stars marks three children whose cheerful surfaces conceal chilling behavior.

title: Bad Taste
note: Peter Jackson’s scrappy debut turns an alien invasion into a deliriously messy splatter-comedy.

title: Q: The Winged Serpent
note: Larry Cohen’s New York monster movie mixes a winged reptile, rooftop danger, and street-level crime.

title: Dead & Buried
note: A small coastal town hides a grim secret in this atmospheric mystery with makeup effects by Stan Winston.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 2: Freddy’s Revenge
note: Freddy Krueger returns as a teenager discovers that the killer’s influence is reaching beyond sleep.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors
note: A group of young patients learns to use their dreams against Freddy in the series’ imaginative third chapter.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 4: The Dream Master
note: The survivors face Freddy again as their dreams become a vivid, effects-packed battleground.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 5: The Dream Child
note: A new generation is drawn into Freddy’s dream world in a surreal continuation of the Elm Street saga.

title: Cat’s Eye
note: A roaming cat links three Stephen King stories in an anthology that balances suspense, dark humor, and creature effects.

title: Lady in White
note: A boy investigates a decades-old disappearance in a nostalgic, atmospheric ghost story set in a small town.

title: Psycho II
note: Norman Bates returns home after years in an institution in a sequel that builds genuine suspense from the original’s legacy.

title: The Hitcher
note: A young driver is pursued across the American Southwest by a mysterious hitchhiker in a lean road thriller.

title: Cannibal Holocaust
note: A controversial Italian exploitation film framed as recovered documentary footage; its production history includes real animal harm.

title: Pulse
note: A radio signal appears to awaken a deadly presence in this atmospheric television horror film.

title: Dark Night of the Scarecrow
note: A rural community’s act of violence returns as a quiet, effective tale of guilt and revenge.

title: Swamp Thing
note: Wes Craven adapts the DC Comics creature into a swamp-set adventure with pulp romance and practical creature work.

title: Cujo
note: A mother and child are trapped in a car by a rabid Saint Bernard in a tense adaptation of Stephen King’s novel.

title: Dolls
note: A storm strands travelers in a mansion where handmade dolls have a life of their own.

title: April Fool’s Day
note: A weekend gathering at a remote island estate becomes a clever, playful mystery with slasher trappings.

title: Waxwork
note: A wax museum’s exhibits become dangerously real in a witty anthology-style creature feature.

title: Lifeforce
note: A space mission returns with an ancient threat in Tobe Hooper’s extravagant blend of science fiction and horror.

title: Maniac Cop
note: A hulking, seemingly unstoppable police officer stalks New York in a gritty cult slasher.

title: Puppet Master II
note: The puppets return to protect their secrets in the first sequel to Full Moon’s killer-puppet series.

title: Puppet Master III: Toulon’s Revenge
note: A wartime prequel reveals how André Toulon and his puppets became enemies of the Nazis.

title: Puppet Master 4
note: A young researcher becomes the target of a demonic force, with Toulon’s puppets caught in the fight.

title: Puppet Master 5: The Final Chapter
note: The story continues directly from Puppet Master 4 as the puppets defend their human ally.

title: Curse of the Puppet Master
note: A sideshow performer discovers Toulon’s puppets and the dangerous secret behind their movement.

title: Retro Puppet Master
note: A prequel travels to Cairo in 1902 to show the beginnings of Toulon’s mysterious creations.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
note: An FBI trainee seeks help from an imprisoned killer while tracking another predator in this landmark psychological thriller.

title: Jacob’s Ladder
note: A Vietnam veteran struggles to understand a series of disturbing visions in a disorienting psychological horror film.

title: Candyman
note: A researcher investigating an urban legend encounters a figure whose story is rooted in a neglected Chicago neighborhood.

title: Scream
note: Wes Craven and Kevin Williamson reinvent the slasher with sharp self-awareness, memorable characters, and a masked caller.

title: Dead Alive
note: Peter Jackson’s splatter-comedy escalates from a mysterious bite to an outrageous suburban zombie outbreak.

title: The Frighteners
note: A small-time paranormal investigator discovers that a grim reaper is haunting his town in this comic supernatural mystery.

title: Cronos
note: Guillermo del Toro’s feature debut follows an antique device that grants its owner a disturbing form of longevity.

title: Mimic
note: Scientists confront an engineered insect species that has adapted to hunt in the New York subway system.

title: Ringu
note: A journalist investigates a cursed videotape in the influential Japanese ghost story that helped define modern J-horror.

title: The Faculty
note: Students suspect an alien presence has taken over their school in a fast-moving science-fiction horror ensemble.

title: Suspiria
note: Argento turns a European dance school into a fever dream of saturated color, sinister architecture, and Goblin’s unforgettable score.

title: Deep Red
note: A pianist witnesses a murder and follows a trail of strange clues through one of Argento’s most intricate, musical mysteries.

title: Inferno
note: A New York apartment building hides occult architecture in this dreamlike, color-drenched chapter of Argento’s Three Mothers cycle.

title: Tenebrae
note: A visiting crime novelist finds his work echoed by a killer. Sleek, self-aware, and packed with Argento’s precise visual flourishes.

title: Opera
note: A young understudy lands a leading role as a masked killer stalks the theater. A grand, operatic late-period Argento set piece.

title: Zombie
note: Released in some territories as Zombi 2, Fulci’s tropical zombie landmark is a slow, eerie, gloriously excessive counterpoint to Romero.

title: City of the Living Dead
note: A priest’s death threatens to open a gateway between worlds in Fulci’s surreal, fog-shrouded first film in the Gates of Hell trilogy.

title: The Beyond
note: A Louisiana hotel is built over one of the seven gateways to Hell. Fulci’s most dreamlike and apocalyptic nightmare.

title: The House by the Cemetery
note: A family moves into a New England home with a murderous history. Patient atmosphere and Fulci’s uncanny sense of place do the damage.

title: The New York Ripper
note: A grimy New York giallo follows a detective hunting a killer who taunts the police. Fulci’s most abrasive urban thriller; viewer discretion advised.
